items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: like when you’re playing with such wonderful players like Warren Vache and Harry Allen, they can read and play through anything.

ctx.x: Uh good question. Okay assuming I’m not the leader I have no clue what’s coming until I get there. So the session usually is booked for two four hour days, 12 to 4 on a Monday, 12 to 4 on a Tuesday. They’re usually consecutive days. And so you turn up at 12 and you might get a bunch of tunes in your hand. You might get a tune for a song. You know what I mean? Like we’re doing this song, here’s the music. Do that song. Here’s the next

song. Here’s — either you know it or they’ll give you a chart you know what I mean? If they’ve got a specific arrangement they’ll always pull a chart. And so if I’m not the leader I have no clue what we’re doing. If I’m the leader and I think the musicians don’t need to know until they get there, you know what I mean, like when you’re playing with such wonderful players like Warren Vache and Harry Allen, they can read and play through anything. You don’t really have to worry about it, you just turn up and you get…
How much control do you get over — I mean you have a producer whose in a sense paying for the session?
